allObjections.title: Unvalidated Claude fix generation
allObjections.detail: §4.1 sends operator source code to Claude with no validation of the fix generation prompt template. A malicious finding could inject prompt instructions via the 'evidence' field, causing Claude to generate destructive diffs that pass syntax checks but introduce backdoors.

allObjections.title: Preview URL crawl amplification attack
allObjections.detail: §6.2 re-runs the full 8-step pipeline including Agent #21's aggressive crawl against every preview URL. A single renewal run could trigger hundreds of crawl requests against the preview, potentially overwhelming Vercel's preview infrastructure or triggering rate limits.

allObjections.title: Branch cleanup race condition
allObjections.detail: §5.7's nightly cleanup job checks for open PRs then deletes branches, but between the PR check and deletion, a new PR could be opened on that branch. The cleanup job lacks atomic branch-deletion-with-PR-check, risking deletion of branches with just-opened PRs.

allObjections.title: Smoke selector injection via admin UI
allObjections.detail: §4.4.1 validates selectors at registry-write time using document.querySelector equivalents, but malicious operators could craft selectors that are valid CSS but execute expensive DOM traversals (e.g., ':has(:has(:has(...)))' deeply nested) causing preview smoke tests to timeout or consume excessive CPU.

allObjections.title: Credential model complexity
allObjections.detail: Section §3.2 introduces a dual credential model with a GitHub App as the default and a PAT fallback. This complexity could lead to security risks if operators do not manage the PATs properly, especially since the PAT fallback can become a long-term default if not monitored.

allObjections.title: Silent-close audit-log bloat
allObjections.detail: Section §6.4 mandates full pre/post/delta payloads in audit logs for silent-close paths. This could lead to significant bloat in the ProductSSOT.governance_record over time, making it difficult for operators to manage and review historical data.

allObjections.title: Phase B graduation criteria
allObjections.detail: Section §4.3 requires a three-condition AND-gate for Phase B graduation, which may be overly restrictive and delay necessary improvements. The criteria could be simplified to ensure timely progression without compromising safety.

allObjections.title: Lack of Human Oversight
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on automated decision-making, which may lead to unintended consequences without sufficient human oversight. Section §4.4 discusses the discard gates, but it is unclear how these gates will be effective in preventing harmful changes.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal mentions testing in §4.4, but it is unclear how comprehensive the testing will be, and whether it will cover all possible scenarios. This lack of testing may lead to regressions or other issues.

allObjections.title: Security Risks
allObjections.detail: The proposal discusses security controls in §8, but it is unclear whether these controls will be sufficient to prevent security breaches. The use of GitHub PATs and Vercel previews may introduce additional security risks.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Phase B Graduation
allObjections.detail: The proposed three-condition AND-gate for Phase B graduation introduces unnecessary complexity. The per-product `selfRenewalScopeRollback` boolean adds to this complexity, making the system harder to manage and understand. Simplifying the graduation process and removing the rollback boolean would make the system more straightforward and easier to maintain.

allObjections.title: Security Risks with PAT Fallback
allObjections.detail: The inclusion of a branch-scoped PAT fallback introduces security risks. Despite the safeguards, using PATs can lead to credential leakage and unauthorized access. Keeping the GitHub App as the only credential model would eliminate this risk and ensure better security.

allObjections.title: Inadequate Delta Policy Validation
allObjections.detail: The cross-field validation for `selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy` and `selfRenewalMinimumDelta` is insufficient. The proposal does not account for scenarios where an operator might want to set a minimum delta threshold that is negative. This could lead to inconsistent behavior and potential misuse of the system.

allObjections.title: Credential Security
allObjections.detail: The proposal's reliance on GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for source acquisition and PR creation introduces a significant security risk. PATs are long-lived and have broad permissions, making them a prime target for attackers. The proposal's mitigation of using branch-scoped PATs and a dedicated machine user is insufficient, as it still requires operators to manually provision and manage these tokens. This increases the attack surface and the likelihood of credential leakage or misuse.

allObjections.title: Limited Scope
allObjections.detail: The proposal limits Phase A to single-file fix generation, which may not be sufficient to address complex issues that require multi-file changes. This limitation could result in incomplete or ineffective fixes, leading to a degraded user experience and reduced trust in the Self-Renewal system.

allObjections.title: Regression Risk
allObjections.detail: The proposal acknowledges that it cannot guarantee that fixes will not introduce regressions. While it includes several gates to catch regressions, such as test suite, typecheck, and preview smoke tests, these gates may not be sufficient to catch all types of regressions. This could result in the deployment of broken code, leading to production issues and a loss of operator trust.

allObjections.title: Credential Rotation
allObjections.detail: The proposal lacks a mechanism for automatic credential rotation.  If a PAT or App key is compromised, there's no automated way to force a refresh across all products using it, requiring manual intervention and potentially leading to prolonged exposure.  This is especially concerning with the PAT fallback.

allObjections.title: Runaway Detection Incompleteness
allObjections.detail: The runaway detector in §4.7 only considers consecutive failures of the *same* gate.  A product could still experience a runaway scenario if it fails different gates consecutively, leading to excessive resource consumption and potentially broken code being proposed without triggering the auto-disable mechanism.  This limits the effectiveness of the runaway protection.

allObjections.title: Lack of Input Validation
allObjections.detail: While the proposal validates CSS selectors at registry-write time (§4.4.1), it lacks sufficient input validation for other operator-configurable parameters.  For example, `githubRepoUrl` is not validated for format or existence, potentially leading to runtime errors and a degraded user experience.  More comprehensive input validation is needed.

allObjections.title: Incomplete Cost Controls
allObjections.detail: While Note 3 acknowledges the cost of re-assessment, the proposal doesn't include any mechanisms to limit the overall cost of Self-Renewal.  There's no budget control or circuit breaker to prevent excessive spending if multiple products experience high finding-throughput, potentially leading to unexpected cost overruns.  The `selfRenewalMaxPerDay` only limits runs, not cost.

allObjections.title: PAT fallback security regression
allObjections.detail: §3.2 reintroduces branch-scoped PAT fallback despite v3 eliminating long-lived tokens. This expands attack surface: PATs stored in Doppler are long-lived credentials vulnerable to exfiltration, contradicting AUTH_TRAVERSAL_SECURITY_SPEC v3 Invariant 2. The 'flowai-self-renewal' machine user with branch-scoped write creates new credential management overhead and potential misconfiguration risks.

allObjections.title: Re-assessment cost explosion
allObjections.detail: §6.2 mandates full 8-step pipeline re-run per renewal, doubling assessment costs. Note 3 estimates $0.65-$5.00/run, unsustainable at scale. No cost-throttling mechanism exists beyond hard rate caps, creating runaway expenditure risk especially for high-finding-density products. This violates CA-9-C cost governance principles.

allObjections.title: Silent-close audit bloat
allObjections.detail: R8 mandates full pre/post/delta payload in governance_record_entry for every silent-close run. §6.4 shows each entry contains 15+ numerical fields. At proposed default settings, high-volume products could generate hundreds of entries weekly, exponentially inflating ProductSSOT storage and degrading query performance without cold-storage strategy.

allObjections.title: Smoke selector runtime fragility
allObjections.detail: §4.4.1 validates CSS selectors at write-time but runtime execution (§4.4c) lacks timeout/retry for dynamic content. Selectors like '#root' may fail during hydration, causing false-positive discards. No error budget for network flakes or Vercel edge-case rendering, making preview-smoke gate unreliable for SSR frameworks.

allObjections.title: PAT fallback reintroduces latent risk
allObjections.detail: Section §3.2 adds `selfRenewalCredentialMode='pat_fallback'` back into Phase A after v3 explicitly removed it. Even with branch-scoping claims, the design depends on branch-protection behavior and a dedicated machine user, which are both easier to misconfigure than the App path and create a long-lived credential surface that the App model avoids.

allObjections.title: Preview-before-PR can deadlock runs
allObjections.detail: Section §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live and smoke-tested before the PR is opened. If Vercel is degraded, the branch is pushed but no PR exists yet, leaving the operator with an invisible in-flight change and forcing a draft PR fallback that contradicts the stated ordering and can confuse review-state semantics.

allObjections.title: Silent-close audit payload may bloat SSOT
allObjections.detail: Section §6.4 / §6.5 mandates full pre/post/delta payloads even when no PR opens. That is useful for transparency, but the proposal stores these as `governance_record_entry` rows on every silent-close path, which can turn routine negative runs into a high-volume history and make ProductSSOT operationally noisy over time.

allObjections.title: Insufficient error handling in source acquisition
allObjections.detail: §3.6 lists 6 abort conditions for source acquisition, but does not specify how these errors are propagated to the operator or handled in subsequent renewal runs. For example, if a PAT scope mismatch occurs (§3.6), the run aborts with 'pat_scope_mismatch', but it's unclear if the operator is notified or if the error is logged for later review.

allObjections.title: Lack of explicit validation for Vercel preview URL
allObjections.detail: §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live before opening the PR, but the validation only checks for HTTP 2xx status. It does not verify the content or functionality of the preview, which could lead to a misleading PR if the preview is broken but returns a 2xx status.

allObjections.title: Unclear handling of consecutive renewal failures
allObjections.detail: §4.7 introduces a runaway detector that disables Self-Renewal after N consecutive same-gate failures. However, it's unclear how this interacts with the hard renewal rate cap (§4.7) or what happens if the operator doesn't re-enable Self-Renewal after auto-disable. For instance, are there any notifications or logs that persist after auto-disable to help the operator diagnose the issue?

allObjections.title: §4.3 Phase B AND-gate undefined
allObjections.detail: The three-condition graduation (≥30 days + zero incidents + new Panel ratification) in §4.3 names no integration point with CANONICAL_REFERENCE §15.1 Agent #3 Executor or §10.2 Human Gates; a new ratification dispatch could bypass the existing Approval gate at 95/95 evaluation.

allObjections.title: §4.7 runaway detector overlaps Self-Audit
allObjections.detail: selfRenewalRunawayThreshold (default 3) auto-disables on consecutive same-gate failures but §10.1 Self-Audit already scores Security Posture 0–10 and triggers Self-Protection; no defined precedence or merge rule between the two auto-disable paths.

allObjections.title: §3.5 Contents API vs Clearance Data Export
allObjections.detail: §3.5 writes via GitHub Contents API after reading Doppler PRODUCT_<id>_GITHUB_PAT, yet CANONICAL_REFERENCE §11 step 4 Data Export must emit full ProductSSOT JSON including governance_record; no scrub or filter prevents PAT metadata leakage into the exported payload.

conditions.topic: Self-Renewal §4.3 v4 R4 — Phase B graduation requires three-condition AND-gate (≥30 days production + zero material incidents + NEW Panel ratification of Phase B spec); per-product `selfRenewalScopeRollback` boolean (default false) allows operators to revert any product back to MAX_FILES=1 even after Phase B ships. Is this the right scope-graduation model?
conditions.draftedText: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.

conditions.topic: Self-Renewal §3.2 v4 R3 — GitHub App as default + branch-scoped PAT fallback behind per-product feature flag `selfRenewalCredentialMode ∈ { app (default), pat_fallback }`. PAT must be branch-scoped to flowai/* via dedicated machine user + branch protection. App permission manifest pinned in-repo at .github/flowai-app-manifest.yml. Is this the right credential model for Phase A?
conditions.draftedText: App-default + opt-in PAT fallback + in-repo manifest is correct — keeps the safe path as default, gives stuck-mid-install operators an escape hatch, and manifest pinning means operators always see permission changes before accepting them.

conditions.topic: Self-Renewal §6.4 v4 R2 + R8 — reverts v3's `selfRenewalOpenPolicy` enum; restores v2 two-field model: `selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy` (ALWAYS_OPEN default | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) + `selfRenewalMinimumDelta` (integer, default 0). Cross-field validation (R2) rejects DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE + selfRenewalMinimumDelta < 0 at registry-write time. Silent-close audit invariant (R8) makes full pre/post/delta governance_record_entry emission a HARD MUST for both discarded_negative_delta and below_threshold paths. Is this the right shape?
conditions.draftedText: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.

conditions.topic: Self-Renewal §6.4 v4 R1 — restores configurability via `ProductRegistry.selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold` (integer, default +5, operator-configurable per product). v3's hardcoded +5 removed. Threshold controls when delta is labelled "substantial improvement" in PR body + audit-log entries. Cross-field validation requires selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta. Is configurable +5-default the right shape?
conditions.draftedText: Configurable integer with +5 default is correct — operators tune "substantial" to their product's value model (e.g. raise to +10 for products where each Five-Layer point is a major win, lower to +3 for high-finding-density products); +5 default preserves a sensible out-of-box meaning.

conditions.topic: Self-Renewal v4 disposition: v4 applies 8 surgical fixes (R1 configurable substantial threshold, R2 two-field model restored, R3 PAT fallback behind per-product flag + manifest, R4 three-condition graduation + scope-rollback, R5 rate cap + runaway detector, R6 nightly branch cleanup, R7 smoke-selector validation at registry-write time, R8 silent-close audit invariant) to address the conditions from v3 NOT_RATIFIED. G-Q2 + G-Q5 carried unchanged. Given all 8 conditions addressed, the appropriate Panel disposition for v4 is:
conditions.draftedText: Promote — the 8 conditions are addressed cleanly and Option C v4 is ready for Phase A engineering dispatch.

objections.title: Smoke selector injection via admin UI
objections.detail: §4.4.1 validates selectors at registry-write time using document.querySelector equivalents, but malicious operators could craft selectors that are valid CSS but execute expensive DOM traversals (e.g., ':has(:has(:has(...)))' deeply nested) causing preview smoke tests to timeout or consume excessive CPU.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The re-assessment cost doubling (§6.2 + Note 3) means every Self-Renewal run costs $0.65-$5.00, and with the default rate cap of 1/day across 5 products, operators could burn $25/day on automated PR generation that they might never merge, versus status quo of manual fixes costing only engineer time.
adversarial.precedent: Dependabot's early versions generated security fix PRs that passed CI but introduced subtle compatibility regressions, leading to 'Dependabot fatigue' where maintainers auto-closed PRs without review - similar risk here with Self-Renewal generating syntactically correct but semantically problematic fixes.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: Self-Renewal v4 introduces significant operational complexity (8 new ProductRegistry fields, dual credential paths, re-assessment costs) while providing no guarantee against regressions (§2, §7.5) and requiring human review of every PR anyway. The engineering effort (3-4 weeks per §9) would be better spent on improving the assessment pipeline's fix hints so developers can implement fixes faster, rather than automating fix generation that still requires full human validation.

G-Q1.pick_text: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.
G-Q1.rationale: The three-condition gate prevents premature authority expansion while the rollback mechanism provides necessary operational flexibility when specific products prove unsuitable for multi-file changes.

G-Q3.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should additionally require PAT fallback usage to expire automatically (selfRenewalCredentialMode auto-reverts to "app" after 30 days of pat_fallback usage), so the fallback can't silently become the long-term default for a product whose operator forgot to flip it back.
G-Q3.rationale: The PAT fallback creates a long-lived credential risk that operators may forget to migrate away from; automatic expiration forces intentional renewal of the less-secure path.

G-Q4.pick_text: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.
G-Q4.rationale: The two-field model provides necessary flexibility while the validation and audit requirements ensure configuration coherence and operational visibility.

G-Q6.pick_text: Wrong validation — requiring selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta is too strict; operators may legitimately want selfRenewalMinimumDelta=5 (open only substantial-or-better PRs) AND selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold=5 (every PR that opens is by definition substantial). Validation should be >=, not >.
G-Q6.rationale: The current validation prevents the reasonable configuration where operators only want PRs for substantial improvements, making every opened PR inherently substantial.

G-Q7.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — the 8 conditions are addressed but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (specify in rationale, non-blocking).
G-Q7.rationale: While R1-R8 are addressed, the spec still has operational concerns around re-assessment costs, lack of regression guarantees, and the G-Q6 validation logic that should be tracked during implementation.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The v4 fixes address the specific R1-R8 conditions but don't resolve deeper concerns about cost amplification and the fundamental value proposition of automated fixes that still require full human review.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal introduces significant complexity in credential management and audit logging, which could lead to security vulnerabilities and operational inefficiencies. The dual credential model with a PAT fallback increases the risk of long-lived token exposure, and the audit-log requirements could result in unmanageable data bloat. These issues suggest that the proposal may need further refinement before implementation.

G-Q1.pick_text: Over-engineered — the per-product selfRenewalScopeRollback boolean is config-creep. Phase B should ship as fleet-wide MAX_FILES=3 with no per-product override; a misbehaving product gets fixed at the engineering level, not patched-around via config.
G-Q1.rationale: The per-product rollback adds unnecessary complexity and could be managed at the engineering level instead.

G-Q3.pick_text: Too permissive — opt-in PAT fallback re-introduces the long-lived-token attack surface that v3 eliminated; Phase A should keep App-only and accept the mid-install friction. The manifest pinning is good and should be kept.
G-Q3.rationale: The PAT fallback reintroduces security risks that were previously mitigated by using the GitHub App exclusively.

G-Q4.pick_text: Wrong invariant on R8 — silent-close audit emissions should NOT include the full preScore/postScore payload; that bloats ProductSSOT.governance_record over time and operators rarely re-read them. Emit only delta + policy; defer pre/post to a separate cold-storage event-log.
G-Q4.rationale: Including full pre/post scores in audit logs could lead to data bloat and inefficiencies in managing historical records.

G-Q6.pick_text: Over-engineered — the substantial-vs-modest label is cosmetic; collapse selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold into selfRenewalMinimumDelta (one field, one knob) and let operators who want a "substantial" label render it client-side in their own dashboards.
G-Q6.rationale: The distinction between substantial and modest improvements is largely cosmetic and could be simplified.

G-Q7.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 8 surgical fixes is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7.rationale: The credential model and audit-log requirements introduce potential security and operational issues that need addressing before promotion.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal's complexity in credential management and audit logging could lead to security and operational challenges that need further refinement.

objections.title: Limited Scope
objections.detail: The proposal limits Phase A to single-file fix generation, which may not be sufficient to address complex issues that require multi-file changes. This limitation could result in incomplete or ineffective fixes, leading to a degraded user experience and reduced trust in the Self-Renewal system.

objections.title: Regression Risk
objections.detail: The proposal acknowledges that it cannot guarantee that fixes will not introduce regressions. While it includes several gates to catch regressions, such as test suite, typecheck, and preview smoke tests, these gates may not be sufficient to catch all types of regressions. This could result in the deployment of broken code, leading to production issues and a loss of operator trust.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the Self-Renewal system introduces regressions or incomplete fixes due to its limited scope, it could result in a worse user experience compared to the status quo, where operators manually review and apply fixes.
adversarial.precedent: The use of long-lived, broad-permission tokens for automated systems has been a common source of security breaches in the past. For example, the 2018 GitHub breach was partially attributed to the misuse of PATs by an attacker.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: Given the significant security risks associated with the use of PATs, the limited scope of Phase A, and the potential for regressions, it would be prudent to reject or defer the proposal until these issues can be adequately addressed. The Panel should consider alternative credential models, such as short-lived, narrowly-scoped tokens, and expand the scope of Phase A to include multi-file fix generation. Additionally, the Panel should ensure that the proposal includes robust regression testing and detection mechanisms to minimize the risk of deploying broken code.

G-Q1.pick_text: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.
G-Q1.rationale: The three-condition AND-gate and per-product rollback mechanism provide a balanced approach to expanding the scope of Self-Renewal, while minimizing the risk of widespread issues.

G-Q3.pick_text: Too permissive — opt-in PAT fallback re-introduces the long-lived-token attack surface that v3 eliminated; Phase A should keep App-only and accept the mid-install friction. The manifest pinning is good and should be kept.
G-Q3.rationale: The use of PATs introduces a significant security risk, and the opt-in PAT fallback mechanism does not adequately mitigate this risk.

G-Q4.pick_text: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.
G-Q4.rationale: The two-field model provides operators with the necessary controls to manage the behavior of the Self-Renewal system, while the cross-field validation and audit-log invariant ensure that the system operates transparently and consistently.

G-Q6.pick_text: Configurable integer with +5 default is correct — operators tune "substantial" to their product's value model (e.g. raise to +10 for products where each Five-Layer point is a major win, lower to +3 for high-finding-density products); +5 default preserves a sensible out-of-box meaning.
G-Q6.rationale: The configurable threshold allows operators to tailor the behavior of the Self-Renewal system to their specific needs, while the default value provides a reasonable starting point.

G-Q7.pick_text: Reject — the 8 fixes expose a deeper architectural problem with Option C that surgical revisions cannot fix; the spec needs ground-up rework or replacement (specify the architectural concern).
G-Q7.rationale: The proposal's reliance on PATs, limited scope, and potential for regressions indicate a need for a more fundamental redesign of the Self-Renewal system.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Self-Renewal system, but it must address the identified security, scope, and regression risks before it can be considered for promotion.

objections.title: Credential Rotation
objections.detail: The proposal lacks a mechanism for automatic credential rotation.  If a PAT or App key is compromised, there's no automated way to force a refresh across all products using it, requiring manual intervention and potentially leading to prolonged exposure.  This is especially concerning with the PAT fallback.

objections.title: Runaway Detection Incompleteness
objections.detail: The runaway detector in §4.7 only considers consecutive failures of the *same* gate.  A product could still experience a runaway scenario if it fails different gates consecutively, leading to excessive resource consumption and potentially broken code being proposed without triggering the auto-disable mechanism.  This limits the effectiveness of the runaway protection.

objections.title: Lack of Input Validation
objections.detail: While the proposal validates CSS selectors at registry-write time (§4.4.1), it lacks sufficient input validation for other operator-configurable parameters.  For example, `githubRepoUrl` is not validated for format or existence, potentially leading to runtime errors and a degraded user experience.  More comprehensive input validation is needed.

objections.title: Incomplete Cost Controls
objections.detail: While Note 3 acknowledges the cost of re-assessment, the proposal doesn't include any mechanisms to limit the overall cost of Self-Renewal.  There's no budget control or circuit breaker to prevent excessive spending if multiple products experience high finding-throughput, potentially leading to unexpected cost overruns.  The `selfRenewalMaxPerDay` only limits runs, not cost.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If a compromised PAT is used to create malicious branches and PRs across multiple repositories before the compromise is detected, the cleanup process could inadvertently delete legitimate branches, causing data loss and disrupting development workflows. This is worse than the current state where no automated branch creation/deletion occurs.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal introduces significant complexity with the PAT fallback and the various configuration options, increasing the risk of misconfiguration and security vulnerabilities. The lack of automated credential rotation and comprehensive cost controls makes the system potentially dangerous and expensive to operate. Deferring the proposal would allow for a simpler, more secure, and cost-effective design to be developed.

G-Q1.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should also require per-finding-category opt-in for multi-file in Phase B (e.g. "this product's accessibility findings can use multi-file, but performance findings cannot"), preventing one bad category from poisoning multi-file authority for an entire product.
G-Q1.rationale: Limiting multi-file changes by category provides finer-grained control and reduces the risk of unintended consequences from broad multi-file changes.

G-Q3.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should additionally require PAT fallback usage to expire automatically (selfRenewalCredentialMode auto-reverts to "app" after 30 days of pat_fallback usage), so the fallback can't silently become the long-term default for a product whose operator forgot to flip it back.
G-Q3.rationale: An automatic expiration for PAT fallback ensures that the more secure App-based approach is prioritized and prevents the fallback from becoming a permanent, less secure solution.

G-Q4.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should expose `selfRenewalMinimumPerLayerDelta` map (per-Five-Layer minima) so an operator can require improvement on a specific layer (e.g. {L1:0,L2:0,L3:0,L4:0,L5:5} means "GTM must improve by 5; other layers may break even") — the single selfRenewalMinimumDelta aggregates over all five and hides layer-specific regressions inside a positive total.
G-Q4.rationale: Per-layer minimum delta provides more granular control over the types of improvements that are considered acceptable, preventing regressions in specific areas from being masked by overall positive scores.

G-Q6.pick_text: Wrong validation — requiring selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta is too strict; operators may legitimately want selfRenewalMinimumDelta=5 (open only substantial-or-better PRs) AND selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold=5 (every PR that opens is by definition substantial). Validation should be >=, not >.
G-Q6.rationale: The current validation is overly restrictive and prevents operators from defining a scenario where all opened PRs are considered substantial improvements.

G-Q7.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 8 surgical fixes is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7.rationale: The lack of automated credential rotation and comprehensive cost controls, as well as the incomplete runaway detection, necessitate further revisions before the proposal is ready for promotion.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is complex and introduces several potential security and operational risks that need to be addressed before it can be safely implemented. The lack of automated credential rotation and comprehensive cost controls are particularly concerning.

objections.title: PAT fallback security regression
objections.detail: §3.2 reintroduces branch-scoped PAT fallback despite v3 eliminating long-lived tokens. This expands attack surface: PATs stored in Doppler are long-lived credentials vulnerable to exfiltration, contradicting AUTH_TRAVERSAL_SECURITY_SPEC v3 Invariant 2. The 'flowai-self-renewal' machine user with branch-scoped write creates new credential management overhead and potential misconfiguration risks.

objections.title: Re-assessment cost explosion
objections.detail: §6.2 mandates full 8-step pipeline re-run per renewal, doubling assessment costs. Note 3 estimates $0.65-$5.00/run, unsustainable at scale. No cost-throttling mechanism exists beyond hard rate caps, creating runaway expenditure risk especially for high-finding-density products. This violates CA-9-C cost governance principles.

objections.title: Silent-close audit bloat
objections.detail: R8 mandates full pre/post/delta payload in governance_record_entry for every silent-close run. §6.4 shows each entry contains 15+ numerical fields. At proposed default settings, high-volume products could generate hundreds of entries weekly, exponentially inflating ProductSSOT storage and degrading query performance without cold-storage strategy.

objections.title: Smoke selector runtime fragility
objections.detail: §4.4.1 validates CSS selectors at write-time but runtime execution (§4.4c) lacks timeout/retry for dynamic content. Selectors like '#root' may fail during hydration, causing false-positive discards. No error budget for network flakes or Vercel edge-case rendering, making preview-smoke gate unreliable for SSR frameworks.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: A product with misconfigured selfRenewalSmokeSelectors experiences consecutive preview-smoke failures, triggering runaway detector auto-disable (R5). The operator misses alerts, leaving findings unaddressed while manual remediation backlog grows. Simultaneously, PAT fallback credentials for another product leak via Doppler compromise, allowing attackers to create malicious 'flowai/renewal-*' branches across repositories before detection.
adversarial.precedent: 2017 GitLab database deletion incident: an automated maintenance script with excessive privileges (analogous to PAT fallback's branch-scoped write) executed destructive operations during production stress, causing catastrophic data loss. Similar privilege overreach risk exists here if branch protections fail.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal introduces unacceptable credential regression (PAT fallback), unsustainable cost model (double assessments), and SSOT-bloating audit trails without solving core limitations like architectural fixes. The 8 fixes add configuration complexity that increases operator cognitive load and failure modes. Defer until: 1) Eliminating PAT fallback entirely 2) Implementing lightweight re-assessment 3) Adding cold-storage for audit logs 4) Proving value in single-file scope before multi-file graduation.

G-Q1.pick_text: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.
G-Q1.rationale: The AND-gate ensures rigorous progression validation, while per-product rollback contains failures without fleet-wide impact.

G-Q3.pick_text: Too permissive — opt-in PAT fallback re-introduces the long-lived-token attack surface that v3 eliminated; Phase A should keep App-only and accept the mid-install friction. The manifest pinning is good and should be kept.
G-Q3.rationale: PAT fallback fundamentally undermines the zero-long-lived-credential principle; installation friction is preferable to credential leakage risks.

G-Q4.pick_text: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.
G-Q4.rationale: The model balances flexibility with coherence checks, and R8's audit guarantee ensures operational transparency.

G-Q6.pick_text: Configurable integer with +5 default is correct — operators tune 'substantial' to their product's value model (e.g. raise to +10 for products where each Five-Layer point is a major win, lower to +3 for high-finding-density products); +5 default preserves a sensible out-of-box meaning.
G-Q6.rationale: Configurability addresses product heterogeneity while +5 default maintains reasonable standardization.

G-Q7.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — the 8 conditions are addressed but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (specify in rationale, non-blocking).
G-Q7.rationale: While fixes satisfy ratification conditions, PAT fallback and cost issues warrant explicit engineering tracking.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Reservations for engineering: 1) Eliminate PAT fallback during implementation 2) Add re-assessment cost projections to operator UI 3) Design governance_record archival strategy.

objections.title: PAT fallback reintroduces latent risk
objections.detail: Section §3.2 adds `selfRenewalCredentialMode='pat_fallback'` back into Phase A after v3 explicitly removed it. Even with branch-scoping claims, the design depends on branch-protection behavior and a dedicated machine user, which are both easier to misconfigure than the App path and create a long-lived credential surface that the App model avoids.

objections.title: Preview-before-PR can deadlock runs
objections.detail: Section §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live and smoke-tested before the PR is opened. If Vercel is degraded, the branch is pushed but no PR exists yet, leaving the operator with an invisible in-flight change and forcing a draft PR fallback that contradicts the stated ordering and can confuse review-state semantics.

objections.title: Silent-close audit payload may bloat SSOT
objections.detail: Section §6.4 / §6.5 mandates full pre/post/delta payloads even when no PR opens. That is useful for transparency, but the proposal stores these as `governance_record_entry` rows on every silent-close path, which can turn routine negative runs into a high-volume history and make ProductSSOT operationally noisy over time.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If preview builds intermittently fail, the system will create renewal branches and spend on fix-generation/tests, but then be unable to open a PR or give the operator a simple review artifact. That is worse than the current status quo of a pure recommendation system, because the operator now has hidden partial state plus cleanup chores without a mergeable output.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub App vs personal access token design tradeoffs are a well-known source of incidents; several GitHub integrations have suffered from over-broad or long-lived token misuse when fallback PATs were introduced. A close real-world analogue is the industry’s repeated migration away from classic PATs toward GitHub Apps and fine-grained tokens because token scope and revocation mistakes caused production exposure; no single exact precedent known for this exact branch-scoped fallback pattern.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this spec is that it expands self-renewal from advisory analysis into a write-capable deployment loop before the surrounding governance and rollback surfaces are mature. The design still depends on multiple brittle external systems—GitHub permissions, Vercel preview readiness, selector validation, and audit-log integrity—and any one misconfiguration can turn a “helpful automation” into an operational burden. Deferring would let the team harden the underlying executor and reduce the chance that the first shipped version creates more review load than it saves.

G-Q1.pick_text: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.
G-Q1.rationale: The additional Panel ratification is the key safety lever; it prevents silent graduation of authority. Per-product rollback is actually useful here because multi-file brittleness can be product-specific, not fleet-wide.

G-Q3.pick_text: App-default + opt-in PAT fallback + in-repo manifest is correct — keeps the safe path as default, gives stuck-mid-install operators an escape hatch, and manifest pinning means operators always see permission changes before accepting them.
G-Q3.rationale: The App should remain the default because it has better revocation and installation semantics. The fallback is risky, but the feature flag and manifest diff at least make the risk visible and intentionally chosen.

G-Q4.pick_text: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.
G-Q4.rationale: This preserves operator control while preventing contradictory settings. The full audit payload is heavy, but it is the right default for traceability on silent-close paths.

G-Q6.pick_text: Configurable integer with +5 default is correct — operators tune "substantial" to their product's value model (e.g. raise to +10 for products where each Five-Layer point is a major win, lower to +3 for high-finding-density products); +5 default preserves a sensible out-of-box meaning.
G-Q6.rationale: A separate substantial-threshold is semantically useful and does not need to be collapsed into the minimum-open gate. The default of +5 is understandable and keeps the label meaningful without forcing tuning.

G-Q7.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — the 8 conditions are addressed but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (specify in rationale, non-blocking).
G-Q7.rationale: The spec meaningfully closes the earlier gaps, but PAT fallback, preview gating, and SSOT verbosity remain real operational risks. These are manageable enough to engineer against, but not trivial enough to ignore.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is directionally stronger than the prior version, but it still crosses several external-system failure boundaries at once. I would not treat it as risk-free; I would ship only with explicit operational monitoring and a quick rollback path for credential mode and preview ordering.

objections.title: Insufficient error handling in source acquisition
objections.detail: §3.6 lists 6 abort conditions for source acquisition, but does not specify how these errors are propagated to the operator or handled in subsequent renewal runs. For example, if a PAT scope mismatch occurs (§3.6), the run aborts with 'pat_scope_mismatch', but it's unclear if the operator is notified or if the error is logged for later review.

objections.title: Lack of explicit validation for Vercel preview URL
objections.detail: §5.5 requires the Vercel preview to be live before opening the PR, but the validation only checks for HTTP 2xx status. It does not verify the content or functionality of the preview, which could lead to a misleading PR if the preview is broken but returns a 2xx status.

objections.title: Unclear handling of consecutive renewal failures
objections.detail: §4.7 introduces a runaway detector that disables Self-Renewal after N consecutive same-gate failures. However, it's unclear how this interacts with the hard renewal rate cap (§4.7) or what happens if the operator doesn't re-enable Self-Renewal after auto-disable. For instance, are there any notifications or logs that persist after auto-disable to help the operator diagnose the issue?

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the runaway detector (§4.7) incorrectly identifies a runaway failure pattern and auto-disables Self-Renewal for a product, the system becomes worse than the status quo because it loses the ability to propose fixes for that product without manual intervention.
adversarial.precedent: A similar design caused problems in the GitHub Dependabot system, where overly aggressive update rules led to frequent breakages and required manual intervention to correct.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal could be rejected or deferred because it introduces multiple complex mechanisms (e.g., source acquisition, fix generation, PR creation, Vercel preview) that interact in non-trivial ways, increasing the risk of unforeseen failures or security vulnerabilities. For example, the use of a fine-grained PAT fallback (§3.2) re-introduces long-lived token risks that were previously mitigated.

G-Q1.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should also require per-finding-category opt-in for multi-file in Phase B (e.g. "this product's accessibility findings can use multi-file, but performance findings cannot"), preventing one bad category from poisoning multi-file authority for an entire product.
G-Q1.rationale: The current three-condition AND-gate is a good start, but lacks granularity to handle different finding categories with varying levels of risk or complexity.

G-Q3.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should additionally require PAT fallback usage to expire automatically (selfRenewalCredentialMode auto-reverts to "app" after 30 days of pat_fallback usage), so the fallback can't silently become the long-term default for a product whose operator forgot to flip it back.
G-Q3.rationale: The PAT fallback is a necessary escape hatch, but without an automatic expiration mechanism, it risks becoming a permanent workaround for operators who forget to switch back to the App.

G-Q4.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should expose `selfRenewalMinimumPerLayerDelta` map (per-Five-Layer minima) so an operator can require improvement on a specific layer (e.g. {L1:0,L2:0,L3:0,L4:0,L5:5} means "GTM must improve by 5; other layers may break even") — the single selfRenewalMinimumDelta aggregates over all five and hides layer-specific regressions inside a positive total.
G-Q4.rationale: The two-field model is a good start, but lacks the granularity to handle layer-specific requirements or regressions.

G-Q6.pick_text: Insufficient — Phase A should expose `selfRenewalModestThreshold` (integer, default +1) so PR-body labels can distinguish "no improvement / modest / substantial" with three bands instead of just "substantial vs not"; operators need finer-grained delta labelling for review-queue triage.
G-Q6.rationale: The current configurable substantial threshold is useful, but having only two labels (substantial vs not) may not provide enough nuance for operators to triage PRs effectively.

G-Q7.pick_text: Promote-with-Reservations — the 8 conditions are addressed but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (specify in rationale, non-blocking).
G-Q7.rationale: While the 8 surgical fixes address the immediate concerns, there are residual issues such as the lack of per-finding-category opt-in for multi-file fixes (§4.3) and the need for finer-grained delta labelling (§6.4) that should be tracked for future improvement.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is generally well-structured, but several areas require additional consideration or refinement to mitigate potential risks or improve operator experience.

objections.title: §4.3 Phase B AND-gate undefined
objections.detail: The three-condition graduation (≥30 days + zero incidents + new Panel ratification) in §4.3 names no integration point with CANONICAL_REFERENCE §15.1 Agent #3 Executor or §10.2 Human Gates; a new ratification dispatch could bypass the existing Approval gate at 95/95 evaluation.

objections.title: §4.7 runaway detector overlaps Self-Audit
objections.detail: selfRenewalRunawayThreshold (default 3) auto-disables on consecutive same-gate failures but §10.1 Self-Audit already scores Security Posture 0–10 and triggers Self-Protection; no defined precedence or merge rule between the two auto-disable paths.

objections.title: §3.5 Contents API vs Clearance Data Export
objections.detail: §3.5 writes via GitHub Contents API after reading Doppler PRODUCT_<id>_GITHUB_PAT, yet CANONICAL_REFERENCE §11 step 4 Data Export must emit full ProductSSOT JSON including governance_record; no scrub or filter prevents PAT metadata leakage into the exported payload.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: A product with selfRenewalCredentialMode=pat_fallback and selfRenewalMaxPerDay=3 could silently accumulate three consecutive preview_smoke_failure runs, auto-disable itself, then still emit a full pre/post/delta governance_record_entry containing the PAT-derived branch name—creating an audit trail that the prior manual-fix workflow never exposed.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal layers eight new per-product registry fields, two credential paths, a nightly cleanup job, and cross-field validation rules on top of an already complex Self-Governance Layer (§10) and Clearance Protocol (§11). Until the existing 26-agent roster and Human Gates have demonstrated stable operation for a full quarter, adding this surface area risks configuration drift and credential-handling regressions that outweigh the incremental benefit of automated PR+preview cycles.

G-Q1.pick_text: Over-engineered — the per-product selfRenewalScopeRollback boolean is config-creep. Phase B should ship as fleet-wide MAX_FILES=3 with no per-product override; a misbehaving product gets fixed at the engineering level, not patched-around via config.
G-Q1.rationale: Adds yet another operator-tunable flag without addressing how rollback interacts with the canonical Human Gates.

G-Q3.pick_text: Too permissive — opt-in PAT fallback re-introduces the long-lived-token attack surface that v3 eliminated; Phase A should keep App-only and accept the mid-install friction. The manifest pinning is good and should be kept.
G-Q3.rationale: Re-opens the exact credential risk the prior revision had closed.

G-Q4.pick_text: Over-engineered — Phase A should ship DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE policy AS THE DEFAULT (not ALWAYS_OPEN); the audit-log invariant is enough to surface negative-delta runs to operators who care, and defaulting to DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE cuts the regression-PR review burden to zero for the long-tail operator who doesn't tune.
G-Q4.rationale: Default ALWAYS_OPEN increases review load without proven operator demand.

G-Q6.pick_text: Wrong validation — requiring selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta is too strict; operators may legitimately want selfRenewalMinimumDelta=5 (open only substantial-or-better PRs) AND selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold=5 (every PR that opens is by definition substantial). Validation should be >=, not >.
G-Q6.rationale: The strict inequality creates an artificial inconsistency for operators who want a single threshold value.

G-Q7.pick_text: Revise — one or more of the 8 surgical fixes is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
G-Q7.rationale: R3 re-introduces PAT surface area and R4 leaves graduation integration undefined; both require further revision.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All objections are drawn directly from cross-references between the proposal and the attached CANONICAL_REFERENCE sections.

questions.topic: Self-Renewal §4.3 v4 R4 — Phase B graduation requires three-condition AND-gate (≥30 days production + zero material incidents + NEW Panel ratification of Phase B spec); per-product `selfRenewalScopeRollback` boolean (default false) allows operators to revert any product back to MAX_FILES=1 even after Phase B ships. Is this the right scope-graduation model?

options.text: Three-condition AND-gate + per-product rollback is correct — Panel re-ratification preserves adversarial review at each authority expansion; per-product rollback bounds blast radius when a specific product turns out to be a poor multi-file candidate.

Insufficient — Phase A should also require per-finding-category opt-in for multi-file in Phase B (e.g. "this product's accessibility findings can use multi-file, but performance findings cannot"), preventing one bad category from poisoning multi-file authority for an entire product.

Over-engineered — the per-product selfRenewalScopeRollback boolean is config-creep. Phase B should ship as fleet-wide MAX_FILES=3 with no per-product override; a misbehaving product gets fixed at the engineering level, not patched-around via config.

Graduation conditions correct but the "material incident" definition (regression revert, credential exfiltration, 5× cost overrun) is too narrow — should also include "operator merge-rate drops below 50% of pre-Self-Renewal baseline" as a material incident, since that signals systemic loss of operator trust.

questions.topic: Self-Renewal §3.2 v4 R3 — GitHub App as default + branch-scoped PAT fallback behind per-product feature flag `selfRenewalCredentialMode ∈ { app (default), pat_fallback }`. PAT must be branch-scoped to flowai/* via dedicated machine user + branch protection. App permission manifest pinned in-repo at .github/flowai-app-manifest.yml. Is this the right credential model for Phase A?

options.text: App-default + opt-in PAT fallback + in-repo manifest is correct — keeps the safe path as default, gives stuck-mid-install operators an escape hatch, and manifest pinning means operators always see permission changes before accepting them.

Insufficient — Phase A should additionally require PAT fallback usage to expire automatically (selfRenewalCredentialMode auto-reverts to "app" after 30 days of pat_fallback usage), so the fallback can't silently become the long-term default for a product whose operator forgot to flip it back.

Too permissive — opt-in PAT fallback re-introduces the long-lived-token attack surface that v3 eliminated; Phase A should keep App-only and accept the mid-install friction. The manifest pinning is good and should be kept.

Wrong shape on the manifest — pinning at .github/flowai-app-manifest.yml inside the FlowAI repo doesn't help operators (they don't read FlowAI's repo); the manifest should be cross-posted to a public FlowAI status page and referenced from the install flow's consent screen instead.

questions.topic: Self-Renewal §6.4 v4 R2 + R8 — reverts v3's `selfRenewalOpenPolicy` enum; restores v2 two-field model: `selfRenewalNegativeDeltaPolicy` (ALWAYS_OPEN default | DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE) + `selfRenewalMinimumDelta` (integer, default 0). Cross-field validation (R2) rejects DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE + selfRenewalMinimumDelta < 0 at registry-write time. Silent-close audit invariant (R8) makes full pre/post/delta governance_record_entry emission a HARD MUST for both discarded_negative_delta and below_threshold paths. Is this the right shape?

options.text: Two-field + cross-field validation + hard audit-log invariant is correct — the two fields give operators independent negative-delta and minimum-improvement controls; the cross-field check eliminates the only incoherent combination; the audit invariant means silent-close is never silent on the audit trail.

Insufficient — Phase A should expose `selfRenewalMinimumPerLayerDelta` map (per-Five-Layer minima) so an operator can require improvement on a specific layer (e.g. {L1:0,L2:0,L3:0,L4:0,L5:5} means "GTM must improve by 5; other layers may break even") — the single selfRenewalMinimumDelta aggregates over all five and hides layer-specific regressions inside a positive total.

Over-engineered — Phase A should ship DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE policy AS THE DEFAULT (not ALWAYS_OPEN); the audit-log invariant is enough to surface negative-delta runs to operators who care, and defaulting to DISCARD_ON_NEGATIVE cuts the regression-PR review burden to zero for the long-tail operator who doesn't tune.

Wrong invariant on R8 — silent-close audit emissions should NOT include the full preScore/postScore payload; that bloats ProductSSOT.governance_record over time and operators rarely re-read them. Emit only delta + policy; defer pre/post to a separate cold-storage event-log.

questions.topic: Self-Renewal §6.4 v4 R1 — restores configurability via `ProductRegistry.selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold` (integer, default +5, operator-configurable per product). v3's hardcoded +5 removed. Threshold controls when delta is labelled "substantial improvement" in PR body + audit-log entries. Cross-field validation requires selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta. Is configurable +5-default the right shape?

options.text: Configurable integer with +5 default is correct — operators tune "substantial" to their product's value model (e.g. raise to +10 for products where each Five-Layer point is a major win, lower to +3 for high-finding-density products); +5 default preserves a sensible out-of-box meaning.

Insufficient — Phase A should expose `selfRenewalModestThreshold` (integer, default +1) so PR-body labels can distinguish "no improvement / modest / substantial" with three bands instead of just "substantial vs not"; operators need finer-grained delta labelling for review-queue triage.

Over-engineered — the substantial-vs-modest label is cosmetic; collapse selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold into selfRenewalMinimumDelta (one field, one knob) and let operators who want a "substantial" label render it client-side in their own dashboards.

Wrong validation — requiring selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold > selfRenewalMinimumDelta is too strict; operators may legitimately want selfRenewalMinimumDelta=5 (open only substantial-or-better PRs) AND selfRenewalSubstantialThreshold=5 (every PR that opens is by definition substantial). Validation should be >=, not >.

questions.topic: Self-Renewal v4 disposition: v4 applies 8 surgical fixes (R1 configurable substantial threshold, R2 two-field model restored, R3 PAT fallback behind per-product flag + manifest, R4 three-condition graduation + scope-rollback, R5 rate cap + runaway detector, R6 nightly branch cleanup, R7 smoke-selector validation at registry-write time, R8 silent-close audit invariant) to address the conditions from v3 NOT_RATIFIED. G-Q2 + G-Q5 carried unchanged. Given all 8 conditions addressed, the appropriate Panel disposition for v4 is:

options.text: Promote — the 8 conditions are addressed cleanly and Option C v4 is ready for Phase A engineering dispatch.
Promote-with-Reservations — the 8 conditions are addressed but the Panel surfaces residual issues that the engineering dispatch should track (specify in rationale, non-blocking).
Revise — one or more of the 8 surgical fixes is incomplete, inconsistent, or introduces a new defect that must be fixed before promotion (specify which condition and the defect).
Reject — the 8 fixes expose a deeper architectural problem with Option C that surgical revisions cannot fix; the spec needs ground-up rework or replacement (specify the architectural concern).
